newsitem.title: UK: April Brent cargoes steady but cash market jumps.
newsitem.headline: April Brent cargoes steady but cash market jumps.

text.p: The North Sea wet Brent crude market charted a steady course on Friday with remaining April barrels moving at unchanged levels, but intermonth spreads and CFDs firmed sharply, traders said.
A cargo loading April 27-29 traded at May Brent -55 cents, following another deals at the same level for a 28-30 loader on Thursday.
The May Brent market looked pressured, with all but one of the cargoes so far nominated from the paper chains clocked. A further five Brents were due to turn wet on Friday.
A May 2-4 cargo clocked on Thursday to a trader was sold in a late pass at quotes related levels.
But the Brent cash market rallied in active trade, with May/June firming by nearly ten cents to trade at -22 cents, while June/July fetched -15 cents.
May Brent was trading 19 cents up at $17.88 a barrel at 1224 GMT.
CFDS also made strong gains with next week trading at June Brent -50 cents, a leap of 10 cents on Thursday's traded levels, and some 25 to 30 cents above Dated Brent values.
Values for other North Sea grades were hard to gauge, with most business in the last few days conducted on a p+c basis.
An early May Draugen traded on Thursday at a fairly steady Dated Brent +3 cents, while one or two Forties were believed to have moved at around Dated Brent +8 cents.
"The grades are basically stuck," said one trader. "We haven't seen the usual jump that grades take each month after the programmes are published."

In a quiet Mediterranean market, Russian Urals was being talked at around Dated Brent -$1.15 to -$1.10 but a European refiner said that at least one cargo had changed hands at Dated Brent -$1.20 to -$1.25 a few days ago.
"Now there's a sort of a wait-and-see attitude, as everybody covered their April needs and for May of course, we are waiting to see cheaper cargoes," the refiner said.
Negotiations between Syrian state oil company Sytrol and term lifters over the May term prices continue with the Syrian's sticking to their initial offer of Dated Brent -82 cents for Syrian Light.
Buyers were hoping for a rollover of the April price of Dated Brent -95 cents, but were expected to pay up to Dated Brent -87 cents.

Negotiations between Algeria's Sonatrach and term lifters for May term prices are going on, with the Algerians "targeting something in the (Dated Brent plus) 50s for Saharan Blend for May", one European lifter said.
He said that the West African market was drawing support from Asian buying.
"I think interest in the Far East, Japan, Korea, Singapore and China, is picking up for West African grades," he said.
